clue.text: Hence a red conspirator, except at the end

indicators.note: this phrase tells us the word for except goes after the conspirator, closing the answer

parts.note: Cinna is one of the plotters against Caesar in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar
bar can mean except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A left-wing plotter is described, with an exception made at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hence a red' is a playful definition: the mineral is the source from which the red pigment vermilion is made.
explanation.definitionFit: This mercury ore is ground to produce vermilion, so a red pigment comes from it.

clue.text: Dart expert capturing second/gold, the aim in some US bars.

definitions.text: the aim in some US bars

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so the expert's name goes around the letter for second

parts.note: Cupid shoots love darts
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A darts champion wins second place and gold, the target in some American bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts S inside CUPID. The definition is a spittoon, once a fixture in American saloons for chewers to aim at.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon was a receptacle in American saloons that tobacco chewers aimed at.

clue.text: It upsets, the rest, making "right mean wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so these two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something that disturbs sleep makes everything feel inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges RIGHT MEAN. The rest upset is a night's sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream disturbs sleep, so it upsets one's rest.

clue.text: Moving a jug

parts.note: jug and stir are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone moving a jug from table to sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug and stir are both British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and about, stirring in motion.

clue.text: In which, a performer has to take a bow

definitions.text: In which, a performer has to take a bow

parts.words: In which, a performer has to take a bow
parts.note: taking a bow sounds like bowing to applause, but here the performer literally picks up a bow to shoot arrows

explanation.definitionFit: Shooting with bow and arrow is the sport in which every competitor must pick up a bow.

clue.text: Wonderful lighthouse

parts.note: the great lighthouse at Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world, and its name became a word for any lighthouse

explanation.definitionFit: The ancient beacon on the island off Alexandria counted among the Seven Wonders, and its name came to mean a lighthouse generally.

clue.text: Endless exaggeration over a double curve

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration

explanation.surface: Unending overstatement about a doubly curved line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final E of HYPERBOLE. 'over' is a link: in a down clue the pieces sit above the A.
explanation.definitionFit: This conic section has two separate branches, a pair of mirror curves.

clue.text: 50 per cent of dirigibles are of this construction

definitions.text: 50 per cent of dirigibles are of this construction

parts.words: 50 per cent of dirigibles are of this construction
parts.note: airships are built either with a stiff frame or as non-framed blimps, so half are framed; the first half of the word dirigibles also holds the letters

explanation.definitionFit: Airships were classed as framed or non-framed, the framed sort being described with this word for stiff.

clue.text: Drink for Mr German's within safety margins

indicators.note: within puts the German title inside the margins
the margins of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Herr is German for Mr

explanation.surface: A drink for Herr Schmidt, kept within safe limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'margins' takes the first and last letters of 'safety', S and Y, and 'within' puts HERR between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Jerez in Spain.

clue.text: Stopped one boy sitting on another

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on puts the first boy above the second

parts.note: Hal is a boy's name, short for Henry
Ted is another boy's name

explanation.surface: One lad sitting on top of another and halting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sitting on' puts HAL above TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to a halt; stopped moving.

clue.text: First for love, second for ESP

definitions.meaning: love at first ... is falling in love on the instant
second ... is a supposed gift of seeing the future, a kind of extrasensory perception

explanation.surface: A ranking puts love at the top and telepathy in second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes two phrases: love at first ___, and second ___, meaning clairvoyance.

clue.text: Charlie's widow

parts.note: '... Charlie' was a music-hall song about a fizz-loving swell, and 'the Widow' is slang for the bubbly of Veuve Clicquot, veuve meaning widow

explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling wine is the drink of the music-hall hero Champagne Charlie, and Veuve Clicquot's 'Widow' is a famous brand of it.

clue.text: Cut section of line caused recent pit disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper line about a mining accident that has severed a railway or power line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges RECENT PIT. In geometry the definition names the part of a line cut off between two points or axes.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this term names the part of a line marked off between two points, such as where it crosses an axis.

clue.text: It spots the bandit coming and going

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever way it travels, forwards or backwards, which is what coming and going describes

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A wartime watcher tracks an enemy aircraft as it arrives and departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandit' is RAF slang for an enemy aircraft; the equipment that detects it is a word spelt the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Detection equipment using reflected radio waves picks out enemy aircraft, which pilots called bandits.

clue.text: Rhetoric in place of prayer

definitions.meaning: the art of public speaking, eloquence
a small chapel for private worship

explanation.surface: Fine speech-making delivered in a chapel, as from a pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the skill of persuasive speaking and a small private chapel.

clue.text: Issue giving 'start of horse-racing season

parts.note: 'they're off' marks the start of a horse race
spring is a season

explanation.surface: A matter arising from the opening of the flat-racing season.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is issue in the sense of children; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Children are a person's progeny, their issue.

clue.text: All of it worked up we hear at Camptown

definitions.meaning: the word means 'it', a thingummy whose name escapes you, and 'all of a' plus it means flustered
the chorus of the song Camptown Races goes '..., ...'

explanation.surface: Everyone gets excited at a racecourse, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Camptown Races is a well-known American minstrel song by Stephen Foster. 'All of a ___' is British slang for agitated, and the same word stands for any unnamed thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The nonsense refrain sung at Camptown also serves as slang for a whatsit, and being 'all of a' one means flustered.

clue.text: He played a lion-tamer and about 100 parts

indicators.note: about puts the word for parts around the numeral

parts.note: roles are parts in a play
the Roman numeral for 100 is C

explanation.surface: An actor's CV: lion-tamer and around a hundred other roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ROLES around C. The definition is a pun: the man in the fable 'played' with a lion, befriending it, as in Shaw's Androcles and the Lion.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fable the slave pulls a thorn from a lion's paw and is later spared by it in the arena, taming it with kindness.

clue.text: May newly-made barons be of humble origin ?

indicators.note: newly made suggests the letters before it are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: Asks whether freshly created peers might come from lowly stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-made' rearranges BARONS BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Born of low or common parentage.

clue.text: Such a beast to betray Samson's riddle!

definitions.text: Such a beast to betray Samson's riddle!

parts.words: Such a beast to betray Samson's riddle!
parts.note: in Judges, Samson tells the Philistines who solved his riddle that they had ploughed with his young cow, meaning they got the answer from his wife

explanation.surface: An exclamation about which animal gave away the strongman's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson's words in Judges 14 call his wife a young cow used for ploughing, the one who leaked his riddle's answer.

clue.text: Wind up again'? Reaction' to being fired

definitions.meaning: the kick of a gun when it goes off

explanation.surface: A gun's kick after firing, like a spring being wound once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as re-coil it means to wind again, and whole it is a gun's backward kick.

clue.text: A patrician lady, possibly a ducal one

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters before it could be arranged another way

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A noblewoman of Rome, perhaps also a duchess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A DUCAL plus I. The Claudii were a patrician Roman family, and its women took the feminine form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Women of the patrician Roman clan of the Claudii bore this feminine family name.

clue.text: Vie with others for cherished income

indicators.note: the word income is split, so in puts the next piece inside the word come

parts.note: taken as written
pet means favourite or cherished

explanation.surface: Fighting over a much-loved salary.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split 'income' into 'in' as the container signal and 'come' as the word that holds the cherished one.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend against rivals.

clue.text: Pinches beer — that's bad !

definitions.meaning: old slang for thin or poor beer

explanation.surface: Someone nicks a pint but finds it is sour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means steals and is also old slang for weak, inferior beer.

clue.text: Doctor goes to work with an eager cry

parts.note: Doctor Who, the time traveller of the BBC television series
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A physician heads to the job shouting with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running British TV science-fiction series, so 'Doctor' gives WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud shout of excitement or delight is this kind of yell.

clue.text: Daggers drawn ?

parts.note: 'at daggers drawn' means hostile, but here the daggers are printed marks drawn by hand in old manuscripts

explanation.definitionFit: These dagger-shaped marks were used in texts to flag doubtful passages or footnotes.

clue.text: Officer's gold-inlaid chest-of-drawers

definitions.note: read as 'officer is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: something inlaid is set into a surface, so the gold goes inside the piece of furniture

parts.note: a commode is an ornate chest of drawers
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A naval officer owns an antique chest decorated with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inlaid' puts OR inside COMMODE. The 's of 'Officer's' stands for 'is' and is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This rank is a naval officer above captain, commanding a squadron.

clue.text: Course of a heavenly sphere, it appears

parts.note: an orb is a celestial globe

explanation.surface: A planet's path is described as it shows up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The path a planet follows round the sun.

clue.text: Cost' about 100p-that is terribly steep

indicators.note: about signals that the word for cost goes around the other letters

parts.note: price is a synonym of cost

indicators.note: terribly suggests a mess, so the letters next to it are scrambled

parts.note: 100 is C in Roman numerals, and p is the penny abbreviation
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something costs around a pound, which is a shockingly steep price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles CP and IE into ECIP, and 'about' wraps the cost word round it. 'Steep' works as a noun here, meaning a steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer cliff face is a very steep drop, and steep as a noun names such a slope.

clue.text: Poor Bob, pierced by the Italian sword

indicators.note: being pierced puts something through the middle, so the Italian article goes inside
poor suggests a bad state, so the name's letters are reworked

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Bob is run through by an Italian's blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the name to BBO, and 'pierced by' slips the Italian article in after the first B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilbo is a Spanish-made sword, named after the city of Bilbao.

clue.text: Drink what the bee gives you, love

parts.note: a bee leaves you a sting
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Advice to have a drink after a bee has stung you, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an old word for a strong, well-aged beer.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word names a strong aged ale.

clue.text: To lose cargo so sounds very black, my lad

indicators.note: so sounds tells us the words that follow, put together and spoken, give the answer

parts.note: jet is very black and a lad of mine is a son; said together they make the spoken word

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned boy is addressed in the language of cargo handling.
explanation.walkthrough: JET (very black) plus SON (my lad), said together, approximates the three-syllable word for throwing cargo overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships dump goods overboard to lighten themselves, which is what this verb describes.
